title: Backward-compatible Linear A transcription IR hardening for cross-surface continuations and unresolved sign-identity conflicts

base.backward_compatibility_rule: A v1.0 IR that does not declare janus_hardening_v1_1 remains governed solely by v1.0. The v1.1 validator first requires a valid sealed v1.0 IR, then validates only the additive hardening extension.

D5.generic_failure_mode: A source-native word or sequence may be split by a physical/surface boundary and must be representable as a continuation relation without destructively merging the original source groups.

D6.generic_failure_mode: A source label and encoded glyph/sign identity may conflict. The label must not silently overwrite glyph identity or acquire semantic authority merely because it appears in a transliteration field.

requirements: source and target group refs resolve to base v1.0 groups
source and target surface refs resolve to distinct base v1.0 surfaces
relation supplies adjacency/continuation evidence but does not create a universal linguistic word claim
disagreement_ref resolves to a base v1.0 disagreement of type SIGN_ID_CONFLICT
at least two assertions with distinct identity values are preserved
each token ref and provenance ref resolves
resolution_state is UNRESOLVED unless the base disagreement itself has a resolved technical status
no source label overwrites source_raw, source_sign_id, or encoded glyph identity

forbidden: silently use source label as sign identity
silently use glyph as source-label identity
assign semantic class from unresolved label/glyph conflict

validation_canaries: claim-bearing scientific view without identity conflict policy fails
base v1.0 fixture remains valid and unchanged under base validator
